title: Solar Phenomena Stretch
welcome_lead: Connect solar activity to space weather, satellites and Earthly impacts.
meta_desc: GCSE Astronomy stretch: space weather, magnetic storms and exam reasoning.
final_note: The Sun's mood swings shape technology and the night sky alike.

concepts.def: Conditions in space affecting Earth and satellites.

walkthroughs.body_html: CMEs can disable satellites, knock out radio communications and induce currents in power grids. Astronauts on the ISS may receive higher radiation doses during storms.
In 1859, the largest recorded solar storm caused telegraph fires and auroras seen as far south as the Caribbean. A repeat today could cost trillions of pounds in damage.
For 'why monitor the Sun' answers: link space weather to satellite damage, power grid impacts, astronaut safety and aviation rerouting. Use 'Parker Solar Probe (2018)' as a named monitoring mission.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a solar eclipse and a lunar eclipse?
options: It is made of fire.
Lunar eclipses are more dangerous.
Solar eclipses happen by day, lunar at night - that is the only difference.
In a solar eclipse the Moon blocks the Sun; in a lunar eclipse Earth's shadow covers the Moon.

mcqs.q: Why don't we have a solar eclipse every new moon?
options: The Moon's orbit is tilted, so it usually passes above or below the Sun's apparent position.
It is made of fire.
Eclipses happen randomly.
Because clouds block them.
